title: Shell Scripting
description: Automate everything — Bash, pipes, control flow, functions and cron.

chapters.title: The Command Line
objectives: Explain the core ideas behind terminal and pwd.
Write and run working Shell Scripting code that uses terminal, pwd, ls.
Recognise and avoid the common pitfalls associated with man.
notes: Note — The Command Line: terminal / pwd / ls / man are the heart of this chapter. Read the sample, then type it yourself.
Good practice: keep every example short and runnable; add a comment that records the expected output exactly.
International standard: every topic points to its section in the appendix and lists revisable key terms at the end.

exercises.question: What is the purpose of terminal in Shell Scripting?
exercises.answer: terminal lets you man — see chapter section 1.2.

exercises.question: Modify the example to keep three decimal places instead of two.
exercises.answer: Format the printed value with the language's precision formatter (e.g. printf/round), then re-run and compare.

exercises.question: When would you avoid man?
exercises.answer: Avoid it when the task is better served by a simpler, linear approach — momentum matters more than cleverness.

tests.instructions: One assessment per chapter grouping plus a final exam. Every question maps to the section shown in brackets so you can revise precisely.

questions.q: Which concept makes terminal behave that way? (Shell Scripting ch.1)
The worked sample prints "Prints working directory then long listing". Which statement caused it? (ch.1)
Which concept makes export behave that way? (Shell Scripting ch.2)
The worked sample prints "Tax is 5%". Which statement caused it? (ch.2)
Which concept makes | behave that way? (Shell Scripting ch.3)
The worked sample prints "Number of words in notes.txt". Which statement caused it? (ch.3)
Which concept makes if behave that way? (Shell Scripting ch.4)
The worked sample prints "Each log plus its line count". Which statement caused it? (ch.4)
Which concept makes function behave that way? (Shell Scripting ch.5)
The worked sample prints "Prints the current year". Which statement caused it? (ch.5)
Which concept makes cron behave that way? (Shell Scripting ch.6)
The worked sample prints "Runs the archive nightly at 02:00". Which statement caused it? (ch.6)
Which concept makes [[ ]] behave that way? (Shell Scripting ch.7)
The worked sample prints "Hello, <current user or guest>". Which statement caused it? (ch.7)

assessment.q: Write Shell Scripting code that reads a value, transforms it and prints the result. (final)
What does the score of 14.3 marks per chapter tell you about this exam's structure? (final)
